source: Co-committed smoke driver, tests and focused how-to
basis: pm-native-local-04.json: strict native CLI requested extension-tool approval despite --allow-tool=pij_send

contract.title: Run extension tool "pij_send"
contract.arguments: Parse only the active bottom modal's single JSON object; require exact expected {to,message}, rejecting extra keys and multiple objects. Prior transcript text never authorizes the dialog.
contract.action: Recheck immediately before one Enter with the exact one-time Yes choice selected; no repeat or session-wide approval.
contract.failure: Unknown/mismatching dialogs fail with PIJ_NATIVE_UNEXPECTED_APPROVAL; no-dialog/stalled-dismissal time out. Never press another key to recover.
contract.evidence: native-tool-human-approval witness records expected pane/recipient/nonce, before, before_confirm, decision, attempted keys, confirmation_sent when the command returns, after_input, after, status and any error. Existing final-pane captures remain unchanged.

typecheck.command: node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit --strict --noUncheckedIndexedAccess --skipLibCheck --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --target ES2022 --esModuleInterop --types node harness/scripts/link-global.ts harness/scripts/link-global.test.ts harness/scripts/copilot-native-fixture.ts harness/scripts/copilot-native-smoke.ts harness/scripts/copilot-native-smoke.test.ts

retained_actual_dialog.result: verifyToolApproval returned true against the retained actual CLI screen

boundaries: PM owns actual live continuation and full gates; neither was rerun here.
No application skipPermission, default grants, blanket permissions, product changes, or tmux message-body delivery.
No new Pi/OMP seats, global links/config/auth changes, machine-daemon changes or toolchain updates.
No full native or real-provider acceptance claimed; unit controls and retained-screen replay are not live successful tool execution.
retrospective: DL-001 encoded: native extension permission UI must be driven as exact per-call simulated human consent, with its own argument block and decision evidence, rather than inferred from command-line allow flags.
